parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes making clean energy the UK's second national mission, targeting clean power by 2030 through a new publicly-owned company called Great British Energy capitalised at £8.3 billion, investment in offshore wind, nuclear and local energy, while banning new oil and gas licences and fracking, and supporting decarbonisation of homes and industry.

citations.quote: To drive forward investment in clean, next parliament. home-grown energy production, Labour will create a new publicly- owned company, Great British Energy
We will not issue new licences to explore new fields because they will not take a penny off bills, cannot make us energy secure, and will only accelerate the worsening climate crisis.

results.headline: Labour pledges clean energy superpower status by 2030
results.quote: Make Britain a clean energy superpower to cut bills, create jobs and deliver security with cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, accelerating to net zero.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives commit to delivering net zero by 2050 through a pragmatic approach, including trebling offshore wind capacity, approving new Small Modular Reactors, maintaining annual oil and gas licensing rounds, and reducing household energy costs, while rejecting what they characterise as Labour's top-down approach.

citations.quote: We will deliver net zero by 2050, by: Sticking to our pragmatic, proportionate and realistic approach that eases the burdens on working people.
We will legislate to ensure annual licensing rounds for oil and gas production from our own North Sea

results.headline: Conservatives promise affordable transition to sustainable energy
results.quote: Delivering an affordable transition to domestic, sustainable energy.

results.headline: Conservative MP: decarbonise affordably without harming communities
results.quote: We believe in decarbonisation, but we need to do it in a way that people can afford and that does not trash our country in the process.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats commit to achieving net zero by 2045 at the latest, proposing a ten-year emergency home energy upgrade programme, a rooftop solar revolution, removal of restrictions on onshore wind and solar, decoupling electricity prices from gas, and restoring the UK's role as a global climate leader through international development spending.

citations.quote: Liberal Democrats are committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2045 at the latest.

Make homes warmer and cheaper to heat with a ten-year emergency upgrade programme, starting with free insulation and heat pumps for those on low incomes, and ensure that all new homes are zero-carbon.

results.headline: Lib Dems commit to net zero by 2045
results.quote: Take the action needed now to achieve net zero by 2045.

results.headline: Lib Dem peer: cost of oil crisis exceeds cost of net zero
results.quote: The Climate Change Committee was clear last week that the cost of another oil price crisis would be greater than the cost of reaching net zero by 2050, so these Benches fully support the need to roll out renewables at a faster rate.
